summary: Full Riftbound test pass: headless tracer invariants + monkey gameplay-flow + per-card playtest on N untested cards. Returns one merged report.

findings.what: After passing priority, Keeper of Masks' play trigger resolved and created two tokens in base, but they appear (in both the snapshot/trace and the AFTER screenshot) as plain 'Reflection' units with 0 Might and definitionId token-def-reflection — not as copies of Keeper of Masks (name Keeper of Masks, 1 Might, cost 2, Hidden, Temporary).
findings.why_wrong: Keeper of Masks (unl-081-219): 'play two Reflection unit tokens here. They become copies of me.' Per rule 477.1.b.1 a copy takes on all copyable traits (name, Might, cost, keywords/abilities; cf. rule 206 example of a Reflection copy having the copied card's cost). The engine registers the per-instance token id as a copy, but server/snapshot.ts resolves name/might/type from cardInstance.definitionId ('token-def-reflection', the shared 0-Might Reflection def) instead of the instance registry entry, so the player is shown two 0-Might vanilla units. Board Might math and the Temporary reminder are therefore misrepresented to the player (and any UI/engine path keyed on definitionId will treat them as 0-Might Reflections).
findings.reason: Trace step 35 shows both tokens as {def:'token-def-reflection', name:'Reflection', might:0}. Engine create-token.ts:121-150 registers each token *instance id* in the global registry as a copy of the source (Keeper of Masks payload, which is registered per-instance via pregame.ts:74/makeLookupPayload), but the shared definitionId 'token-def-reflection' is registered at create-token.ts:101-109 with the literal 0-Might Reflection stats. server/snapshot.ts:366-368 resolves `def` only via `registry.get(cardInstance.definitionId) ?? getGlobalCardRegistry().get(cardInstance.definitionId)` — never by instance id — so lines 397-398 emit might 0 / name 'Reflection' instead of the copy's Keeper of Masks traits.

findings.what: The two Reflection tokens created by Keeper of Masks sit in base as name='Reflection', might 0, def 'token-def-reflection' (trace base[] and boardById), and render as generic 'Reflection' placeholders / generic token art rather than as Keeper of Masks. Keeper itself shows might 1.
findings.why_wrong: Keeper of Masks (unl-081-219): 'When you play me, play two Reflection unit tokens here. They become copies of me.' The tokens should present as copies of Keeper of Masks (name, 1 Might, Hidden/Temporary). The engine's create-token registers the per-instance copy in the card registry, but the snapshot/UI resolves the token via the shared 'token-def-reflection' definition, so the player sees (and might/combat display uses) 0-Might vanilla tokens. Pre-existing state, still visibly wrong after this step.
findings.reason: Trace step 36 base[] shows two tokens with def 'token-def-reflection', name 'Reflection', might 0, while Keeper of Masks shows might 1. Source: create-token.ts:101-109 registers shared 'token-def-reflection' with literal tokenDef stats (Reflection, might 0); create-token.ts:142-150 registers the per-instance copy of the source card only under the instance tokenId. effect-context.ts:85-89 stamps the instance's definitionId as `token-def-<slug>`. snapshot.ts:366-368 resolves `def` via cardInstance.definitionId (the shared token-def-reflection), and lines 397-398 take might/name from that def — so the UI/snapshot shows vanilla 0-Might Reflection instead of a Keeper of Masks copy.

findings.what: After End Turn advanced to player-1's turn 5, Keeper of Masks and its two Reflection token copies were correctly killed by Temporary at the start of the Beginning Phase, but the global trash count went 0 -> 3: the two Reflection tokens (ids token-reflection-*) were placed in the trash and remained there for the whole of turn 5's main phase (trace step 38 later shows trash=1, i.e. they were only swept on a subsequent cleanup pass).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 186.1: a token put into any non-board zone other than the chain ceases to exist immediately after moving there. The engine's sweepOffBoardTokens (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts) evidently did not run after the Temporary kill in the Beginning Phase, so for an entire turn the tokens are real trash-zone objects that trash-referencing effects (e.g. Cemetery Attendant 'return a unit from your trash to your hand', currently in a hand this game) could see/choose.
findings.ruleOrCard: 186.1 (tokens cease to exist off-board) / Keeper of Masks (unl-081-219) Temporary + Reflection tokens
findings.reason: The Beginning-phase Temporary kill (riftbound-flow.ts:364-367) does a bare `context.zones.moveCard({cardId, targetZoneId:"trash"})` for every Temporary permanent, tokens included, and nothing in the beginning/channel/draw/main onBegin hooks calls performCleanup/runStateMaintenance afterwards (grep: no cleanupAndFireDeaths/runStateMaintenance/removeCardFromGame anywhere in riftbound-flow.ts). The only token sweep is sweepOffBoardTokens at cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:72-87, invoked from performCleanup step 0 (line 252), which runs via the withPostMoveCleanup wrapper inside the move reducer. In core rule-engine.ts the reducer (line 571) executes before the deferred flow transitions (pendingPhaseEnd -> flowManager.nextPhase at line 623-635), so endTurn's post-move cleanup fires before the next turn's Beginning phase, and the tokens trashed by Temporary sit in the trash until the next move triggers cleanup. Trace matches: step36 base has Keeper + 2 token-reflection-*, trash=0; step37 (turn 5 main) trash=3; step38 (after next End Turn move) trash=1.

findings.what: On End Turn (step 38) the combined trash zone shrank from 3 cards to 1 with no effect that banishes/returns cards from trash having been played (Goldfish opponent played nothing; P2 hand grew by exactly its draw, board unchanged). The 3 trash cards at step 37 were Keeper of Masks plus its two Reflection unit tokens, killed by Temporary at the start of turn 5; the two tokens sat in the trash zone for the entire turn-5 main phase and were only swept when the next cleanup pass ran during the turn transition (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts sweepOffBoardTokens runs only at the start of a later performCleanup).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 186.1: a token put into any non-board zone other than the chain ceases to exist immediately after moving there. Reflection tokens must not persist in the trash across a whole turn — while there they inflate trash counts and are visible/selectable to trash-referencing effects (e.g. P2's Cemetery Attendant 'return a unit from your trash', Gust Monk 'banish a card from any trash'), and their delayed removal makes the trash pile visibly shrink on an unrelated End Turn.
findings.ruleOrCard: 186.1 (tokens cease to exist off-board) / Keeper of Masks Reflection tokens
findings.reason: Rule 186.1 verified ("If a token is put into any Non-Board Zone besides the chain, it ceases to exist immediately"). The Beginning-phase Temporary kill in riftbound-flow.ts:327-368 does `context.zones.moveCard({cardId, targetZoneId: "trash"})` (line 364-367) for every Temporary permanent, tokens included, with no token-existence handling and no cleanup pass afterwards in the flow hook. The only implementation of 186.1 is sweepOffBoardTokens (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:72-87), invoked solely as "Step 0" of performCleanup (line 251-254), which in turn only runs via post-move cleanup (withPostMoveCleanup -> cleanupAndFireDeaths -> runStateMaintenance) or chain/choice resolution. endTurn's reducer (moves/turn.ts:98-101) just calls flow.endPhase(); the post-move sweep runs before the next turn's Beginning-phase kill, so the tokens trashed there persist until the next move. Trace matches: step 36 base = Keeper of Masks + 2 Reflection tokens, trash 0; step 37 (turn 5 main) base = Noxian Emissary only, trash 3; step 38 (turn 7 main) trash 1, board unchanged, hands grew only by draws, goldfish played nothing — the 2 tokens sat in trash through turn 5 and were removed only when the End Turn move's cleanup pass ran.

findings.what: In the AFTER screenshot (opponent's Turn 6 Beginning Phase, Loose Cannon trigger on the chain, banner 'Goldfish has Priority — waiting...'), the player's action panel still offers 'Exhaust Rune (4 available)' and 'Recycle Rune (4 available)' as available actions.
findings.why_wrong: Rune Exhaust/Recycle are Reaction-speed Add abilities; per 429.3 they may be activated only when the player has priority or is in a pay-costs window. Player-1 has neither while the opponent holds priority on its own Beginning-Phase trigger, so these actions should not be presented as available.
findings.reason: Screenshot 38.png verified: Turn 6 BEGINNING, chain shows Loose Cannon (Goldfish ability), banner 'Goldfish has Priority — waiting...', and player's Rune Actions panel lists 'Exhaust Rune (4 available)' / 'Recycle Rune (4 available)'. Source cause: engine move `exhaustRune.condition`/`enumerator` (resources.ts:71-117) and `recycleRune.condition`/`enumerator` (resources.ts:141-195) only check pendingChoice, status==='playing', zone===runePool, ownership, and exhausted flag — no check of turn/priority/chain state. Line 79 comment explicitly states 'Players can exhaust runes at any time' (same at line 149). The UI (apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/actions.js:344-415) renders whatever the engine enumerates with no priority gating. Rules: 164.2.a/b make rune abilities [Reaction] Add abilities; 312.1.a/b say only the player with Priority may take discretionary actions/activate abilities; 429.3 carves out only the pay-costs window. Player-1 has neither here, so offering these moves is a rules deviation rooted in the engine condition.

findings.what: Static clause "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities unless I'm in combat" is not implemented — enemy spells can choose Akali while she is not in combat.
findings.expected: With Akali at a battlefield in a NON-combat showdown (isCombatShowdown:false, combatRole:null, no enemy units present), player-2's Hextech Ray ("Deal 3 to a unit at a battlefield") should not be able to choose Akali as a target (only the other friendly unit Sneaky Deckhand should be offered).
findings.observed: GET /moves?player=player-2 listed playSpell Hextech Ray with targets:[Akali]; executing it succeeded, chain item resolved and Akali took 3 damage (meta.damage=3, lastDamageSource=spell). parseAbilities(rulesText) returns only the move trigger — the conditional untargetable clause is dropped entirely (no static/restriction ability), and target-resolver isUntargetable() only checks unconditional Untargetable grants.
findings.reason: Running parseAbilities on Akali's rulesText yields only the move-to-battlefield trigger; the "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities unless I'm in combat" clause produces no ability. The parser's only self "can't be chosen" pattern (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-grant-keyword.ts:198-200) is anchored `...abilities\s*(this turn)?\.?$` so the trailing "unless I'm in combat" fails to match, and static-parser.ts:1305-1307 only handles the Alpha Wildclaw form. VEN cards are built from ven.json via parseAbilities (data/all-cards.ts:839-840, enrich-cards.ts:30) with no per-card override for ven-038-166. Engine-side, isUntargetable (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/target-resolver.ts:507-536) only honors printed keyword, unconditional static grant-keyword (condition === undefined), or meta.grantedKeywords — none of which exist for Akali — so enemy Hextech Ray can choose her out of combat.

findings.what: [Exhaust] ability targets units instead of "another gear".
findings.expected: activateAbility for Hextech Formula should offer other gear (e.g. Seal of Discord in base) as targets, exclude units and itself, and resolving should set empowered on the chosen gear.
findings.observed: Enumerated activateAbility (abilityIndex 1) offered only targets:[Gem Jammer] (a unit); forcing targets:[Seal of Discord] was rejected with CONDITION_FAILED. Chain item effect was {type:'empower', target:{type:'unit'}} and on resolution the unit Gem Jammer got meta.empowered=true while the Seal gear was untouched. parseAbilities yields effect.target {type:'unit'} for 'Empower another gear'.
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-resources.ts:191-210 (parseEmpowerEffect) matches "another gear" but routes it to parseCardTarget (parser/impl/targets.ts:13-27), which hardcodes `{ type: "unit" }` and never inspects "gear" or "another" (no excludeSelf). Running parseAbilities on Hextech Formula's rulesText yields activated effect `{target:{type:"unit"}, type:"empower"}`, so the engine targets units, rejects gear, and empower.ts sets meta.empowered on the chosen unit. ven.json has abilities:[null], so the runtime parser output is what is used.

findings.what: Main effect 'Move an enemy unit to a battlefield where you have units' resolves to a non-existent zone
findings.expected: On resolution the targeted enemy unit moves to a battlefield where player-1 has units (prompting for which one if several); the 'where you have units' restriction limits legal destinations
findings.observed: Parsed effect is {type:'move', target:{unit,enemy}, to:'battlefield'} (literal string, no 'where you have units' filter, no destination choice). When both players pass, resolution fails with {error:'Target zone battlefield does not exist', errorCode:'EXECUTION_ERROR'} (seen on REST passChainPriority for player-2; goldfish auto-pass silently fails the same way).
findings.reason: Reproduced. ven-148-166 (Shadow Dash) has `abilities:[null]` in packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:4323 and is runtime-parsed (all-cards.ts getAllCards) to `{type:"move", target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy"}, to:"battlefield"}` — no "where you have units" filter, no destination choice, and the "+1 Might if exactly two units" rider is dropped. In packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/move.ts:530-541, a string `to` that isn't "chosen-battlefield"/"target-battlefield"/"choose"/"same"/"here" is used verbatim as the zone id (`targetZone = dest` → moveCardWithEvent(ctx, id, "battlefield")), and core zones.moveCard throws `Target zone battlefield does not exist` (packages/core/src/operations/operations-impl.ts:225). Harness repro: P1 casts Shadow Dash targeting an enemy unit at bf2, P1 passes, P2 pass → `passChainPriority rejected: Target zone battlefield does not exist`; spell stays stuck on chain, foe never moves.

findings.what: Failed resolution is non-atomic and soft-locks the game
findings.expected: If an effect throws, state is unchanged (unit stays in base) or the spell fizzles and the chain clears
findings.observed: After the failed resolve, the targeted enemy Recruit token disappeared from every zone (base [] and not in trash/banishment/any battlefield — 113 cards, none is the token), while the chain item stayed active with activePlayer=player-2; every subsequent passChainPriority returns the same EXECUTION_ERROR, UI shows 'Goldfish has Priority — waiting...' forever. Only Rewind recovers.
findings.reason: ven-148-166 is re-parsed at load (all-cards.ts:808-810) into `{type:"move", target:{unit,enemy}, to:"battlefield"}` (verified via bun). In riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/move.ts:530-541 a plain-string `to` that isn't a special keyword becomes targetZone="battlefield" and is passed straight to ctx.zones.moveCard; no such zone exists (zone-configs.ts only defines base/battlefieldRow/`battlefield-${id}` etc.). core operations-impl.ts:192-226 moveCard splices the card out of its source zone (line 203) BEFORE checking the target and throwing `Target zone battlefield does not exist` (line 225). These zone ops mutate engine.internalState directly (rule-engine.ts:487-490), which is outside the immer produce; the catch at rule-engine.ts:676-706 returns EXECUTION_ERROR without restoring internalStateBefore (snapshot at :565 is only used for undo). Net: unit removed from every zone, game state (chain item/priority) rolled back unchanged, so each subsequent pass/resolve re-throws the same error -> soft-lock; only undo/Rewind restores internalState (:1240-1242).

findings.what: 'If you have exactly two units there, they each get +1 Might this turn' clause is not implemented
findings.expected: Parsed ability includes a conditional follow-up granting +1 Might this turn to each of the two friendly units at the destination
findings.observed: Enriched card abilities contain only the move effect and the Flow keyword; no conditional might buff exists in the chain item effect. (Could not observe at runtime either since resolution crashes.)
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:4305 defines ven-148-166 (Shadow Dash) with abilities:[null]; runtime enrichment via getAllCards() yields only [{type:'spell', effect:{type:'move', target:{type:'unit',controller:'enemy'}, to:'battlefield'}}, {type:'keyword', keyword:'Flow', cost:{energy:5,power:['rainbow','rainbow']}}]. No conditional '+1 Might if exactly two units' effect exists; parser has no handling for 'exactly two' (grep in src/parser and enrich-cards.ts returns nothing) and no TS override for this card id exists.

findings.what: Spell is offered/playable with no legal destination
findings.expected: With zero friendly units at any battlefield there is no 'battlefield where you have units', so the spell should not be playable (or should require a legal destination)
findings.observed: playSpell for Shadow Dash targeting the enemy Recruit was enumerated while player-1 had no units at any battlefield (only enemy token in base).
findings.reason: Card ven-148-166 has no hand-authored def; it is parsed at runtime from rulesText via the flexible fallback in /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-move.ts:239-262, whose regex `(?:\s+to\s+(...|a battlefield|...))?(?:\s+.*)$` swallows " where you have units..." and emits `{type:"move", target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy"}, to:"battlefield"}` with no friendly-units destination filter (verified via getAllCards()). Engine-side, chosenMoveDestinations (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/targeting.ts:498-540) returns undefined for a plain-string `to:"battlefield"`, so play-spell.ts:427-432 applies no destination restriction. Empirical repro with harness: 2 battlefields, P1 has zero units anywhere, P2 has one unit in base -> game.p1.legal() lists "cast Shadow Dash [dash]" and enumerateMoves(playSpell, validOnly) returns {cardId:"dash", targets:["enemy"], isValid:true}. (Resolution then also fails with "Target zone battlefield does not exist".)

findings.what: 'The first time I win a combat each turn, you score 1 point.' never fires
findings.expected: Draven (6 might) attacked bf with an enemy Recruit token (1 might), won the combat and conquered: player-1 should score 2 (1 conquer + 1 from Draven's win-combat trigger)
findings.observed: player-1 VP went 0->1 (conquer only); no chain item/trigger, log only 'Combat resolved'. Root cause: parseAbilities(rulesText) yields only [Deflect keyword, {type:'spell', effect:{type:'score',player:'opponent',amount:1}}] — no win-combat triggered ability; additionally engine never emits a 'win-combat' event from resolve-full-combat (repo has a test.failing acknowledging this).
findings.reason: parseAbilities on Draven's rulesText yields only [Deflect keyword, {type:'spell', effect:score opponent 1}] — no win-combat trigger; packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:40 only matches /^When I win a combat,/ so 'The first time I win a combat each turn' is unparsed. Additionally, grep shows no non-test emitter of a 'win-combat' GameEvent anywhere in riftbound-engine (only type decls at abilities/game-events.ts:85, trigger-matcher.ts:149, events/dispatcher.ts:97), and __tests__/core-rules/combat-flow-and-resolution.test.ts:216 is a test.failing acknowledging the engine never emits win-combat.

findings.what: 'When I die in combat, choose an opponent. They score 1 point.' never fires
findings.expected: Draven (6 might, 3 prior damage) defended vs two attacking Mech tokens (3+3); all units died (tie). Draven died in combat -> prompt to choose an opponent (or auto-pick the only opponent) and player-2 scores 1 point
findings.observed: Draven moved to trash, battlefield uncontrolled, player-2 VP stayed 0; no pendingChoice, no chain item. Parsed abilities contain no die-in-combat trigger (the sentence was mis-parsed into a bare 'spell' score-opponent effect).
findings.reason: draven-audacious.ts:4-18 declares no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:30 runs parseAbilities on rulesText at load. Running the parser on the exact rulesText yields only [{keyword:"Deflect"}, {type:"spell", timing:"action", effect:{type:"score", player:"opponent", amount:1}}] — no triggered ability with a die/die-in-combat trigger (and the win-combat trigger is dropped too). With no death trigger on the card, the engine has nothing to fire when Draven dies in combat, matching the observed no pendingChoice / no chain item / VP unchanged.

findings.what: "I don't deal combat damage" is not honored in combat resolution
findings.expected: Ezreal (3 Might, alone) attacking a lone 3-Might enemy Mech token: Mech deals 3 to Ezreal (Ezreal dies), Ezreal deals 0 combat damage so the Mech survives undamaged.
findings.observed: After resolveFullCombat both Ezreal AND the Mech were removed (Ezreal to trash, Mech token gone; battlefield empty). Ezreal's card meta shows grantedKeywords:[{keyword:'NoCombatDamage',duration:'static'}] but combat-resolver.ts only sets dealsNoCombatDamage for stunned units / Vilemaw threshold; the 'NoCombatDamage' keyword is never consulted in resolve-full-combat.ts, so Ezreal contributed his full Might as combat damage.
findings.reason: Ezreal (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/ezreal-dashing.ts:49-54) grants itself keyword "NoCombatDamage", but the engine never consults that keyword: grep for "NoCombatDamage" in riftbound-engine/src returns zero hits. CombatUnit.dealsNoCombatDamage is set only for stunned units (game-definition/moves/combat/resolve-full-combat.ts:337-341) and the Vilemaw PreventWeakerEnemyCombatDamage threshold (combat/combat-resolver.ts:152-166); calculateSideMight (combat-resolver.ts:136-145) skips only units with that flag, so Ezreal contributes full Might and kills the Mech.

findings.what: Defiant Dance applies both the +2 and the -2 to the same unit instead of two different units
findings.expected: Chosen unit A gets +2 Might this turn and a different unit B gets -2 Might this turn (two distinct targets; 'another unit' excludes the first)
findings.observed: Played via UI (click card -> one target prompt -> Pouty Poro/Overzealous Fan): spell went on chain with targets=[one id]; after resolution the target had meta.mightModifier=0 and might stayed 2 (i.e. +2 and -2 both landed on it), the other friendly unit had no modifier at all, and no pendingChoice/second prompt ever appeared. Forcing two targets via executeMove(playSpell,{targets:[A,B]}) resolved with BOTH units at mightModifier 0 (each sub-effect applied to every target) instead of A=+2/B=-2. Parsed effect is sequence[modify-might +2 target{type:unit}, modify-might -2 target{type:unit}] with no per-effect target binding / excludeSelf.
findings.reason: Parser (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-might.ts:143-186) matches the compound "Give X +N ... and another Y -M" pattern but swallows "another" in a non-capturing group, emitting sequence[modify-might +2 target{type:unit}, modify-might -2 target{type:unit}] with identical descriptors and no excludeBound (verified by running parseAbilities on the card text). In the engine, collectSequenceTargetSlots (game-definition/moves/play/targeting.ts:147-171) merges identical descriptors via isRestatementOf into ONE slot, so findSequenceLeadTarget yields a single play-time target prompt. handle_sequence (abilities/effects/sequence.ts:69-80) only routes per-slot when slots.length >= 2, so ctx.boundTargets=[A] is threaded to both steps and getTargetIds (_helpers.ts:49-50) returns the bound id for each -> +2 and -2 both land on A; with targets [A,B] both steps receive both ids. No card-level override exists for sfd-196-221.

findings.what: Only one target is requested when playing Defiant Dance
findings.expected: Targeting flow asks for two units (first for +2, then 'another unit' for -2); move enumerator offers two-target combinations
findings.observed: availableMoves lists playSpell variants with a single-element targets array only (one per unit); UI banner 'Choose a target for Defiant Dance' closes after one click and the spell is immediately put on the chain with 1 target. With zero units on board the spell is not offered at all, with exactly one unit it is offered (should need two distinct units).
findings.reason: Parser drops "another": in packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-might.ts:144 the compound regex consumes `another` in a non-capturing group `(?:another\s+)?` before capture group 5, so parseTarget(compoundMatch[5]) (line 173) gets bare "unit" and never sets excludeSelf. Verified by running parseAbilities on the card text: sequence of two modify-might effects both with target {type:"unit"} (identical). The engine's collectSequenceTargetSlots (packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/targeting.ts:165) then treats the second identical descriptor as a restatement of the first and merges them into ONE slot, so findSequenceLeadTarget returns a single lead target and the playSpell enumerator (play-spell.ts:748-785) emits single-target variants only; the sequence handler threads that one bound target to both steps. Hence one-target prompt, offered with exactly one unit on board.

findings.what: "Choose ... a spell" — no choice of which spell to counter when 2+ spells are on the chain
findings.expected: With Right of Conquest (cost 3) and Flurry of Blades (cost 1) both on the chain, playing Riposte should prompt for which spell to counter (rule 425.3: Counter [a card or ability on the chain]) — either per-target playSpell moves or a pendingChoice — and the Might bonus should follow the chosen spell's cost
findings.observed: playSpell moves for Riposte only enumerated the friendly-unit target (one move per friendly unit, no spell parameter); no pendingChoice appeared at play or resolution. Engine silently countered the most recent spell (Flurry of Blades -> trash) and gave +1 Might; Right of Conquest stayed on the chain. Card def encodes a bare {type:"counter"} with no target selector.
findings.reason: Riposte's def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/riposte.ts:17-27) is a `sequence` of a bare `{type:"counter"}` (no target) + `modify-might` targeting a friendly unit. Play-time enumeration in play-spell.ts only offers a per-chain-item choice when the TOP-LEVEL effect is `counter` (play-spell.ts:1186-1207, `else if (spellEffect?.type === "counter")`). For a sequence, collectSequenceTargetSlots (targeting.ts:147-171) skips sub-effects with `target === undefined` (line 159), so the only slot is the friendly-unit descriptor; findSequenceLeadTarget returns it, isCardTarget is true (play-spell.ts:787-798 — checks `spellEffect?.type !== "counter"`, which is "sequence" here), and the isCardTarget branch (line 987) enumerates one Play per friendly unit with no spell parameter. At resolution handle_counter (abilities/effects/counter.ts:47-67) reads boundTargets[0] = the unit id, finds it is not on the chain (boundOnChain false), and falls back to the topmost legal spell — silently countering the most recent spell with no pendingChoice. Matches the observed behavior.

findings.what: Cannot click the friendly-unit target in the UI while the chain modal is open
findings.expected: After clicking Riposte in hand (banner 'Choose a target for Riposte' shown, base units get class valid-target), clicking a base unit should select it
findings.observed: The 'The Chain' modal (#chainBox, z-index 1500) sits directly over the player's base zone; elementFromPoint at the unit's center returns .chain-pass-btn, and a real click on the unit times out. Only a synthetic dispatched click (or executeMove) could complete targeting. Same after using the sidebar 'Play Spell Riposte' button.
findings.reason: The chain overlay is `position:fixed; inset:0; align/justify center; z-index:1500` (public/css/gameplay.css:678-688) and while visible its `.chain-box` keeps `pointer-events:auto` (gameplay.css:694). The box is unscaled (~290px tall with one chain item: title/subtitle/72px item/priority/Pass button/hint) and centered on the viewport, whereas the board is a 1920x1080 logical canvas scaled down to fit; the player-base row sits directly beneath the vertically-centred battlefield row, so the lower part of the box (where .chain-pass-btn lives) lands over #player-base units. The only mitigation for board-pick prompts is `.chain-overlay.targeting { justify-content:flex-end }` (gameplay.css:1784-1790), but that class is toggled exclusively on #choiceOverlay in renderPendingChoiceModal (render/modals.js:32,41,179) — never on #chainOverlay. Client-side targeting mode entered from hand/sidebar (interactions.js:357-361 adds body.targeting-mode; banner text at interactions.js:321) has no CSS or JS that hides/moves #chainBox (targeting-mode rules at gameplay.css:1748-1750 only style cards). So with the chain open and Riposte's 'Choose a target' banner up, real clicks on base units under the box hit .chain-pass-btn/.chain-box instead of the .valid-target card.

findings.what: Repeat execution is dropped when the chosen mode opens a choose-target prompt.
findings.expected: Played with repeatCount:1 (paid 4+1=5 energy). After resolving the first 'Choose one' (picked mode 3: -4 Might, then picked Noxus Saboteur from a 2-unit choose-target prompt), a second choose-mode prompt with the remaining modes [0,1,2] should appear (rule 820.1.d: execute the instructions one additional time).
findings.observed: After resolvePendingChoice {pickedCardId: Saboteur} the -4 was applied (meta.mightModifier=-4) but pendingChoice became null and no further prompt/effect occurred — only one execution for a paid repeat. findings.what: 'Each player must kill one of their units' resolves as a single choose-target prompt for the controller covering ALL units (friendly and enemy); only one unit dies and the opponent never kills one of theirs.
findings.expected: Player-1 chooses and kills one of player-1's units; separately player-2 must kill one of player-2's units (Recruit token). Two kills total, each restricted to that player's own units.
findings.observed: pendingChoice {type:choose-target, playerId:player-1, options:[Legion Rearguard(p1), Safety Inspector(p1), Recruit(p2)], remaining:1}. findings.reason: Safety Inspector (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/safety-inspector.ts) has no hand-authored abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:30 runs parseAbilities. The parser branch at riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:143-154 emits `{player:"each", target:{type:"unit"}, type:"kill"}` with NO `controller:"friendly"` (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText). The engine only routes to the per-player kill loop when `isEachPlayersOwn` is true, which requires `tgt.controller === "friendly"` (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/kill.ts:97-105, dispatch at :175-179). So it falls through to plain `killUnits(getTargetIds(...))`, a single controller-owned choose-target over all units (friendly+enemy), one kill, opponent never prompted — exactly matching the observation. Contrast Cull the Weak (ogn-209-298) which hand-authors `controller:"friendly", quantity:{upTo:1}` and works. (Also unhandled: the "if you paid my additional cost, you don't kill" clause is dropped by the parser.)

findings.what: Paying the optional 3 XP additional cost does not exempt the controller from the kill.
findings.expected: With paidAdditionalCost=true (XP 4->1 was deducted), player-1 should not be asked to kill a unit; only player-2 kills one of theirs (Mech token).
findings.observed: Trigger went on chain with triggerEvent.paidAdditionalCost:true but the effect was identical: pendingChoice for player-1 with options [Recruit(p1), Safety Inspector(p1), Mech(p2)], remaining:1 — player-1's own units still offered/required; no automatic kill for player-2.
findings.reason: Safety Inspector (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/safety-inspector.ts) has no hand-authored abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:30 derives them from parseAbilities(rulesText). Running the parser on the card text yields only `{type:"kill", player:"each", target:{type:"unit"}}` on play-self — the sentence "If you paid my additional cost, you don't kill a unit this way" is silently dropped (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:144-154 matches "Each player must kill one of their units" and returns a bare target with no controller and no paid-additional-cost conditional). In the engine, kill.ts:97-105 `isEachPlayersOwn` requires `target.controller === "friendly"`, so this effect falls through to the plain path kill.ts:179 `killUnits(getTargetIds(...))`, which resolves `{type:"unit"}` against all units of both players -> pendingChoice for player-1 with [Recruit(p1), Safety Inspector(p1), Mech(p2)], remaining:1, exactly as observed. Nothing in kill.ts or the trigger path consults triggerEvent.paidAdditionalCost to exempt the controller (the only consumer, trigger-runner.ts:308, evaluates a `paid-additional-cost` condition the parser never emitted). Contrast ogn-209-298 (cull-the-weak.ts) which hand-authors `controller:"friendly"` to hit the per-player path.

findings.what: Yi's 'While you have 8+ runes' +4 Might is not re-evaluated when the rune pool shrinks via recycleRune (or after exhaustRune); the stale +4 persists until some unrelated move runs cleanup/static recalculation.
findings.expected: After recycling a rune from 8 down to 7 runes, staticMightBonus should drop to 0 immediately (Might 4).
findings.observed: At 8 runes staticMightBonus=4/UI shows 8 (correct). After recycleRune (REST result success, p1 runes=7, chaos power +1) staticMightBonus stayed 4 and UI still showed 8; also unchanged after a subsequent exhaustRune. Only after playing another unit did it recompute to 0. recycleRune/exhaustRune reducers in moves/resources.ts do not run post-move cleanup (recalculateStaticEffects).
findings.reason: recycleRune reducer (packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/resources.ts:196-214) only calls zones.moveCard + increments pool.power; exhaustRune reducer (resources.ts:118-130) only sets the exhausted flag + energy. Neither invokes performCleanup/recalculateStaticEffects nor is wrapped in withPostMoveCleanup (only movement.ts:24, counters.ts, pending-choice.ts, dispatcher do). The 'runes-at-least' condition (abilities/static-abilities.ts:178-183) is only evaluated inside recalculateStaticEffects, so staticMightBonus stays stale. Reproduced with audit harness: 8 runes + Yi-style static -> might 8/staticMightBonus 4; applyMove recycleRune (success, runes=7) -> might still 8, staticMightBonus 4; exhaustRune -> still 8; manual recalculateStatics -> 4.

findings.what: Optional additional cost 'you may discard 1' and the 'deal 5 instead' rider are missing
findings.expected: playSpell should offer a paidAdditionalCost variant (discard 1 from hand) like other discard-additional-cost cards (e.g. ogn-002-298), and when paid the spell should deal 5 instead of 3

findings.reason: Card data at /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:549-568 (ven-008-166 Ruthless Strike) has "abilities": [null] despite rulesText declaring "As an additional cost to play this, you may discard 1 ... If you paid the additional cost, deal 5 to it instead." No TS card override exists (grep for ven-008-166/ruthless-strike finds only the JSON). play-spell.ts:262-263 and :1220 gate the paidAdditionalCost variant on getOptionalPlayCost(cardId) (cost.ts:780-896), which reads registry abilities and needs an additional-cost-option ability; ran a harness scenario and got getGlobalCardRegistry().getAbilities("ven-008-166") -> [] and getOptionalPlayCost -> undefined, so no paid variant is enumerated and forcing paidAdditionalCost fails the condition. findings.what: Abandon does not let the player choose which spell to counter when multiple spells are on the chain
findings.expected: With Mobilize (chain-2) and Premonition (chain-3) both on the chain, playing Abandon should prompt for a target spell (per-target playSpell variants or a pendingChoice) so the player can pick either Mobilize or Premonition to counter
findings.observed: playSpell for Abandon was offered with no targets param and no pendingChoice appeared; chain item had no target recorded ({type:'counter',destination:'hand'}). On resolution it auto-countered the topmost spell (Premonition, returned to hand) — no way to counter Mobilize instead
findings.reason: Abandon's rulesText is parsed at load (enrich-cards.ts) into a `sequence` effect: [{type:'counter',destination:'hand'},{type:'predict',amount:1}] (verified by running parseAbilities). The play-spell enumerator only emits per-chain-item target variants when the TOP-LEVEL effect is a counter: play-spell.ts:1186 `else if (spellEffect?.type === "counter") { ...baseVariants.push({targets:[key]}) }`; a sequence falls through to the `else` at ~1207 which pushes a variant with no targets. Likewise isCounterSpell at play-spell.ts:390 checks only top-level type. With no boundTargets, handle_counter (abilities/effects/counter.ts, loop `for (let i = items.length-1; i>=0; i--)`) picks the topmost legal spell, so Premonition is auto-countered and Mobilize can never be chosen. Bare "Counter a spell" cards (e.g. ogn-064) work because their effect is a top-level counter; Abandon's trailing [Predict] wraps it in a sequence and bypasses the targeting branch.

findings.what: Deathknell trigger target is chosen at resolution instead of when the trigger is finalized onto the chain
findings.expected: Per rules 337.1/340.4 the pending Deathknell item should be finalized (enemy-unit target chosen) before any player receives priority, so the opponent can react knowing the target
findings.observed: After Rex died, chain item chain-3 {damage 4, target:{controller:enemy,type:unit}} sat on the chain with no `targets` and pendingChoice=null while passChainPriority was the only move; the choose-target prompt (options = both enemy units) only appeared after priority was passed and the item began resolving
findings.reason: trigger-target-lock.ts:85-107 deliberately skips early target locking for non-duplicated triggers: it builds a `duplicated` set of same-card/same-effect trigger keys and `if (duplicated.size === 0) return;` (line 105-107), with the comment "A lone pending trigger is equivalent whether it chooses now or at resolution, and the engine's convention is to prompt at resolution." So a single Ruined Rex Deathknell item is left on the chain with no `targets` and no pendingChoice, and the choose-target prompt is only raised by the damage effect at resolution. Rules 337.1/355.5/383.3 require the Pending triggered item to be Finalized (Game Object chosen) before priority passes (340.4), and 383.4.b.2 targeting-effects depend on that timing, so the "equivalent" assumption is wrong and the observed behavior is a genuine engine deviation.

findings.what: Spiderling's '+1 Might for each other unit you control here with my name' is applied as a flat +1 regardless of how many other Spiderlings share its location
findings.expected: Lone Spiderling: +0 (might 1). Two Spiderlings at same location: +1 each. Three Spiderlings at the same battlefield: +2 each (might 3).
findings.observed: meta.staticMightBonus was 1 in every configuration: a single Spiderling alone in base (others still in hand) had staticMightBonus=1; one at battlefield + one at base (different locations) each had 1; all three together at battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-276-298 each still had staticMightBonus=1. Parsed ability is {type:static, effect:{type:modify-might, amount:1, target:self, per:"other unit you control here with my name"}} — the `per` string is not evaluated, so amount is applied once unconditionally.
findings.reason: Parser emits {type:"modify-might", amount:1, per:"other unit you control here with my name", target:"self"} at packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/parsers/static-parser.ts:616-634 for "I have +N [Might] for each QUALIFIER". The engine's applyStaticEffect (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/static-abilities.ts:515-585) only handles numeric amount, {cardsInTrash}, {count}, and {score}; a numeric amount is used verbatim (line 518-519) and `effect.per` is never read anywhere in riftbound-engine/src (grep for `.per`/"per" returns nothing). So Spiderling always gets staticMightBonus = +1 regardless of how many same-named units share its location (should be 0 alone, N-1 with N together).

findings.what: Deathknell sequence order inverted: the 'draw 2' executes before the 'Discard 2' choice is made
findings.expected: Per rulesText 'Discard 2, then draw 2': player picks and discards 2 cards from the current hand first; only after that are 2 cards drawn (player must not see the drawn cards when choosing discards)
findings.observed: On resolving the Deathknell chain item, deck went 35->33 and hand 5->7 (Legion Rearguard + Chemtech Enforcer / Seal of Rage + Doran's Ring drawn) immediately, and only then a pendingChoice {type:'reveal-and-pick', onPicked:'discard', remaining:2} appeared. The pick list was restricted to the 5 pre-draw hand cards (so net card outcome matches), but the draw visibly happened before the discard decision, leaking information and contradicting the 'then' ordering.
findings.reason: Undercover Agent has no hand-authored abilities (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/undercover-agent.ts), so enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText; for "[Deathknell] — Discard 2, then draw 2." effect-keyword-parser.ts:240-250 emits `{type:"sequence", effects:[{discard 2},{draw 2}]}` (verified by running parseAbilities) rather than a discard with a `then` clause. handle_sequence (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/sequence.ts:268) executes each step in turn; handle_discard (effects/discard.ts:53-66) parks a `reveal-and-pick` pendingChoice (revealed = pre-draw hand, then = undefined) and returns, but sequence.ts:276-288 only suspends remaining steps when the parked choice is `choose-mode`, so the loop proceeds and runs the draw step immediately while the discard prompt is still pending. This exactly produces the observed draw-before-discard ordering with the pick list limited to the pre-draw hand.
